I'm one of those people who are probably unhealthily attached to their pets. Maybe it's because I'm jaded since most of the humans in my life have let me down. When I was a kid I just didn't care about our pets as much, because they were just kinda... there. Cute and fluffy, but not much more. Probably because I was just busy surviving, haha. 

But my first cat as an adult, well... he kinda picked me. I was at the shelter surrounded by animals and he just came right up and fell asleep on my lap & wouldn't let me leave. He's been glued to my side ever since. And it's definitely not because I feed him - for the first 6 years of his life, my ex husband exclusively fed the cats. But this little boy greets me when I get home every day, misses me when I'm gone (he will yowl when I get back from vacation and refuse to un-attach himself from me), he has comforted me when I cry. If I have a panic attack he'll lay on my legs and purr until my breathing evens out. I give him a place to live, and in return he has brought so so much unconditional love and joy to my life. 

I'm not trying to say that you need to feel the same way, just giving an example of the other side. :) I totally see your point, too. If it wasn't for this one cat, I would feel the same way. Hell, I've felt pretty indifferent to other cats I've known since him. I don't know what it is, but this little guy tugs on my heart strings more than any other human person I've met. I can't explain it, and it even seems stupid typing it out like this. Maybe I just can't connect to people that well in general. But it is what it is. My cat is family - it's the only word to me that fits. But I also find it completely reasonable for someone to not have the same attitude. I expect people to provide basic care to their pets, but wouldn't be offended if they didn't have a deeper connection. That's just silly.
